name: laptop-health-monitor
description: 24/7 laptop hardware, OS, and performance monitoring system with intelligent diagnostics, alerting, and historical tracking for Arch Linux on i7-12650H + RTX 3050
conventions: Modular collectors with isolated failure domains
No GPU usage for monitoring itself
All external commands wrapped with timeout + error handling
Metrics collected at 30s interval, aggregated to 5m/1h/1d
SQLite WAL mode for concurrent reads during writes
Configuration via TOML file, not env vars
Structured logging to SQLite + rotating text logs
No external network calls for core monitoring
All alerting via local webhook/Telegram only
Enforce Arch Linux On-Demand System Rulebook (SYSTEM_RULEBOOK.md)
All background services must be strictly on-demand with clean exit cleanup
architecture_patterns: Each collector is a standalone module with well-defined output schema
Diagnostic engine uses rule-based + heuristic analysis (no LLM by default)
Watchdog monitors collectors via systemd + PID file

patterns: Unit tests for each collector with mocked sysfs/proc
Load tests simulating high resource usage
Chaos tests: kill collectors, remove sensors, fill disk

sprint_focus: Build core collectors, storage, diagnostic engine, and dashboard
never_do: Never use GPU for monitoring computations
Never auto-kill processes or modify system config
Never collect passwords, tokens, browser data, or private content
Never fabricate metrics when sensors unavailable - mark as unknown
Never use heavy frameworks (no Prometheus, Grafana, InfluxDB, k8s)
Never run as root - use sudo only for specific commands (smartctl, nvme)
Never block on external network calls in collectors
Never log secrets or personal data
Never claim system is 'error-free' - only report verified state
Never install packages without explicit confirmation
Never enable unsolicited boot or background daemons
Never bypass D-Bus circuit breakers or autostart shields
preferred_patterns: Use dataclasses + type hints for all metric schemas
Use context managers for resource cleanup
Use asyncio for I/O-bound collectors (journalctl, network)
Use threading for CPU-bound collectors (psutil, sensors)
Prefer /sys and /proc reads over shell commands
Batch SQLite writes, use WAL mode
Implement circuit breakers for flaky data sources
